A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GANQ work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. v1's outlier-extraction and additional-results appendices are retained as Appendices B and C in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, including perplexity, six zero-shot task accuracies, and GPU latency and memory measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds LongBench/GSM8K evaluations, LLaMA-3.2 results, preconditioning sensitivity measurements and outlier-handling profiles.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the residual-update factor from L[j:,j] to L[j:,j-1], locally correcting the written procedure. The alternating optimizer, objective and outlier extraction remain intact. Adaptive preconditioning is newly specified, but the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments used a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v3 adds LongBench long-context evaluation and GSM8K mathematical reasoning (Table 4), substantially extending task requirements beyond the retained perplexity datasets and six original zero-shot tasks. No original dataset coverage is removed.

E2.justification: The profiling comparison removes GPTQ and GPTQ (g128) and adds GANQ's outlier-handling variant, GANQ-star (v1 Table 5 versus v3 Table 6). The original accuracy-comparison sets remain unchanged; extending RTN, GPTQ and OmniQuant to new evaluations does not introduce new comparator methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B base and Instruct configurations, zero-shot evaluation without chain-of-thought prompting for the new tasks, and a fixed-lambda preconditioning sweep. Existing calibration budgets, bit widths and hardware remain unchanged. Explicit batch-size and evaluation-length statements are additional disclosures, not established protocol revisions.

E4.justification: New Appendix A compares five fixed regularization values against adaptive preconditioning on 4-bit OPT-125M, directly testing sensitivity (Table 7). The expanded profiling also measures the runtime and memory costs of outlier handling, complementing its already reported accuracy benefits.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both primarily present point estimates; the zero-shot mean averages tasks rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: Original accuracy-table values remain unchanged after matching renumbered tables. v3 adds substantial LongBench/GSM8K and LLaMA-3.2 results plus preconditioning measurements. For example, newly reported 3B-Instruct GSM8K accuracy is 60.50% for GANQ versus 54.74% for OmniQuant. Profiling adds GANQ-star measurements and removes GPTQ measurements; these are added or removed results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v3 adds a first-order derivation of the existing codebook update and adaptive-preconditioning equations with a positive-definiteness argument. It also replaces the norm-expansion inequality and upper-bound description with equality and restricts Remark 3.1 to nonzero vectors. These are local mathematical additions and corrections, without a new convergence theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: optimization-based, GPU-adaptive non-uniform quantization, improved 3-bit/4-bit accuracy, outlier compatibility and up to 2.57-fold speedup. The introduction clarifies kernel attribution without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the uniform-quantization slowdown discussion and untested 3-bit GPTQ extrapolation with an explicit accuracy/runtime tradeoff for GANQ-star and attribution to existing LUT kernels. New passages interpret preconditioning insensitivity, baseline failures on the added tasks, and adaptation to differing weight distributions.

D1.justification: v3 reports a public implementation and supplies a repository link absent from v1. It newly specifies profiling batch size 1, perplexity evaluation length 2,048, and the adaptive diagonal-offset formula with a 10^-8 floor. Existing calibration sample counts, hardware and iteration-count information are retained.

R1.justification: A new LUT-kernel discussion explicitly distinguishes quantizer development from kernel engineering and adds Guo et al. Other additions cover LongBench, GSM8K, LLaMA-3.2 and solver documentation; the GPTQ-for-LLaMa reference is removed. Publication updates for retained works do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v3 locally expands method explanations and related work, rewrites profiling discussion, corrects OmniQuant spelling, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. A new Appendix A shifts the existing appendices to B/C, while the main narrative order and most original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4, 7 and 10, revises the profiling table's rows and caption, and adjusts table rules and highlighting. Existing figures, algorithms and tables are relocated or resized within the retained two-column layout; there is no wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Broader task validation, a targeted sensitivity study, clearer implementation details and reported code access strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. Kernel attribution and outlier-handling costs are clearer. These gains are tempered by removing GPTQ latency comparisons and Appendix A's incorrect general claim that weak diagonal dominance with positive diagonal guarantees positive definiteness, making the net improvement modest.
